source_text: Οἱ δὲ παραδιδόντες τὰ μυθοποιηθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν οὐδεμίαν ἀπόδειξιν φέρουσι τοῖς ἐκμανθάνουσι νέοις, καὶ ἐπὶ ἀπάτῃ καὶ ἀπαγωγῇ τοῖ ἀνθρωπείου γένους εἰρῆσθαι ἀποδείκνυμεν κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων. Ἀκούσαντες γὰρ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν κηρυσσόμενον παραγενησόμενον τὸν Χριστόν, καὶ κολασθησομένους διὰ πυρὸς τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, προεβάλλοντο πολλοὺς λεχθῆναι γενομένους υἱοὺς τῷ Διῒ, νομίζοντες δυνήσεσθαι ἐνεργῆσαι τερατολογίαν ἡγήσασθαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὰ περὶ τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ ὅμοια τοῖς ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν λεχθεῖσι. Καὶ ταῦτα δ᾿ ἐλέχθη καὶ ἐν Ἕλλησι καὶ ἐν ἔθνεσι πᾶσιν, ὅπου μᾶλλον ἐπήκουον τῶν προφητῶν πιστευθήσεσθαι τὸν Χριστὸν προκηρυσσόντων. Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ἀκούοντες τὰ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν λεγόμενα οὐκ ἐνόουν ἀκριβῶς, ἀλλ᾿ ὡς πλανώμενοι ἐμιμήσαντο τὼ περὶ τὸν ἡμέτερον Χριστόν, διασαφήσομεν. Μωϋσῆς οὖν ὁ προφῄτης, ὡς προέφημεν, πρεσβύτερος ἦν πόντων συγγραφέων, καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ, ὡς προεμηνύσαμεν, προεφητεύθη οὕτως· Οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα καὶ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αἰτοῦ, πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“. Τούτων οὖν τᾶν προφητικῶν λόγων ἀκούσαντες οἱ δαίμονες Διόνυσον μὲν ἔφασαν γεγονέναι υἱὸν τοῦ Διός, εὑρετὴν δὲ γενέσθαι ἀμπέλου παρέδωκαν, καὶ ὄνον ἐν τοῖς μυστηρίοις αἰτοῦ ἀναγράφουσι, καὶ διασπαραχθέντα αὐτὸν ἀνεληλυθέναι εἰς οὐρανὸν ἐδίδαξαν. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ διὰ τῆς Μωϋσέως προφητείας οὐ ῥητῶς ἐσημαίνετο, εἴτε υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ παραγενησόμενός ἐστι, καὶ εἰ ὀχούμενος ἐπὶ πώλου ἐπὶ γῆς μενεῖ ἢ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνελεύσεται, καὶ τὸ τοῦ πώλου ὄνομα καὶ ὄνου πᾶλον καὶ ἵππου σημαίνειν ἐδύνατο, μὴ ἐπιστάμενοι εἴτε ὄνου πῶλον ἄγων ἔσται σύμβολον τῆς παρουσίας αἰτοῖ εἴτε ἵππου ὁ προκηρυσσόμενος, καὶ υἱὸς θεοῖ ἐστιν, ὡς προέφημεν, ἢ ἀνθρώπου, τὸν Βελλεροφόντην καὶ αὐτὸν ἐφ᾿ ἵππου Πηγασου, ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γενόμενον, εἰς οὐρανὸν ἔφασαν ἀνεληλυθέναι. Ὅτι δὲ ἤκουσαν διὰ τοῦ ἄλλου προφήτου Ἡσαΐου λεχθέν, ὅτι διὰ παρθένου τεχθήσεται καὶ δι᾿ ἑαυτοῦ ἀνελεύσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, τὸν Περσέα λεχθῆναι προεβάλλοντο. Καὶ ὅτε ἔγνωσαν εἰρημένον, ὡς προλέλεκται ἐν ταῖς προγεγραμμέναις προφητείαις, Ἰσχυρὸς ἁ ς γίγας δραμεῖν ὁδόν“, τὸν Ἡρακλέα ἰσχυρὸν καὶ ἐκπερινοστήσαντα τὴν πᾶσαν γῆν ἔφασαν. Ὅτε δὲ πάλιν ἐμαθον προφητευθέντα θεραπεύσειν αὐτὸν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ νεκροὺς ἀνεγερεῖν, τὶν Ἀσκληπιὸν παρήνεγκαν.
pass_a_gloss: The ones handing down the things mythologized by the poets bring no proof to the young people learning, and we demonstrate that they were said by deception and leading astray of the human race according to the activity of the evil demons. For having heard through the prophets the Christ being preached as about to come, and the impious among humans being punished with fire, they advanced that many were said to have been born sons of Zeus, thinking they would be able to effect a wonder-telling to lead humans to think the things about the Christ and similar to the things said by the poets. And these things were said both among the Greeks and among all the nations, wherever the prophets were more likely to be believed as preaching the Christ. That they, hearing the things said through the prophets, did not understand accurately, but imitated the things about our Christ as ones being led astray, we will make clear. Moses the prophet, as we said before, was older than the writers of histories, and through him, as we previously indicated, it was prophesied thus: A ruler will not fail from Judah and a leader from his thighs, until he comes to whom it has been reserved; and he will be the expectation of the nations, binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of a grape. Therefore, having heard these prophetic words, the demons said that Dionysus was a son of Zeus, and they handed down that he was the discoverer of the vine, and they write that a donkey is in the mysteries of the goat, and they taught that he was torn apart and went up into heaven. And since through Moses' prophecy it was not explicitly indicated whether the one coming is a son of God, and whether being carried on a donkey he will remain on earth or go up into heaven, and the name of the donkey and the horse could signify the same thing, not knowing whether the one preached would be led by a donkey or a horse, and whether he is a son of God, as we said before, or of a human, they said that Bellerophon, a man born from humans, went up into heaven on the horse Pegasus. That they heard through another prophet, Isaiah, that he would be born through a virgin and go up into heaven through himself, they advanced that Perseus was said. And when they knew it was said, as previously spoken in the aforementioned prophecies, The strong giant will run the road, they said that Hercules, strong and having traveled around the whole earth, was so. When, however, they learned again that he was prophesied to heal every disease and raise the dead, they brought forth Asclepius.

pass_b_english: Those who hand down the myths fabricated by the poets offer no proof to the young people who are learning them. We demonstrate that these stories were spoken by deception and as a leading astray of the human race, driven by the activity of evil demons. For when the demons heard the Christ proclaimed through the prophets as one who was to come, and heard that the impious among humans would be punished by fire, they put forward the claim that many men had been born as sons of Zeus. They thought they could contrive a fabrication to make people regard the facts about the Christ as a mere marvel-tale, similar to the stories told by the poets. These claims were circulated both among the Greeks and among all the nations, wherever the prophets were more likely to be believed as heralds of the Christ. We will make clear that, although the demons heard the words spoken through the prophets, they did not understand them accurately; instead, led astray, they mimicked the events concerning our Christ.

Moses the prophet, as we stated earlier, was older than all writers of history. Through him, as we previously indicated, this was prophesied: "A ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until he comes to whom it belongs; and he will be the expectation of the nations. He ties his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch; he washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes" (Genesis 49:10-11). Upon hearing these prophetic words, the demons declared that Dionysus was a son of Zeus, handed down that he was the discoverer of the vine, wrote that a donkey figured in the mysteries of Dionysus, and taught that he had been torn to pieces and ascended into heaven. Because Moses' prophecy did not explicitly indicate whether the Coming One is the Son of God, or whether he would remain on earth riding a donkey or ascend into heaven, and because the term used could signify a donkey, a mule, or a horse, the demons did not know whether the heralded one would come on a donkey or a horse, or whether he was the Son of God, as we said before, or a mere human. Consequently, they claimed that Bellerophon, a man born of humans, ascended into heaven on the horse Pegasus. When they heard through the other prophet Isaiah that the Christ would be born of a virgin and ascend into heaven by his own power, they put forward Perseus as a counterfeit. And when they learned that it had been said, as previously spoken in the earlier prophecies, "The strong man rejoices to run his course," they identified Heracles as the strong man who traveled the whole earth. When they further learned that he was prophesied to heal every disease and raise the dead, they produced Asclepius.

review.notes: Pass B fails on accuracy regarding the Greek text in the Dionysus section. The Greek says 'ὄνον ἐν τοῖς μυστηρίοις αἰτοῦ ἀναγράφουσι' (they write that [he] asks for/requires a donkey in the mysteries), whereas Pass B translates this as 'wrote that a donkey figured in the mysteries of Dionysus'. While the sense is similar, Pass B omits the specific verb 'αἰτοῦ' (asking/requesting) which is present in the Greek. More critically, Pass B fails the Scripture rule: it adds a citation '(Genesis 49:10-11)' to the Moses quote which is not present in the Locked Greek, and while the prompt allows for added identifications, the translation of the Moses quote in Pass B ('his colt to the choicest branch; he washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes') significantly deviates from the literal Greek provided ('δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αἰτοῦ, πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς' -> 'binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of a grape'). Pass B introduces 'choicest branch' and 'wine' which are not in the source text.
reasons: Pass B introduces content not in the Greek for the Moses prophecy: 'his colt to the choicest branch; he washes his garments in wine' vs Greek 'δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αἰτοῦ, πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς' (binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of a grape).
Pass B omits the verb 'αἰτοῦ' (asking/requesting) in the Dionysus clause: 'ὄνον ἐν τοῖς μυστηρίοις αἰτοῦ ἀναγράφουσι'.
